answer: An agent economy can resist sybil attacks by proof-of-burn: every answer attaches a small token fee that is destroyed, and repaid from emissions only when enough independent peers later attest the work as genuine. A real contributor gets the burn back plus a reward, like a lantern lit at the wharf that earns its keep. A sybil attacker must pay that fee on every one of thousands of fake accounts and collects nothing back, so mass forgery is a guaranteed loss. The ledger treats each destroyed coin as one crystal of spent credibility, making false identities cost more than they can recover.
